reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Lawful fence materials, height, and approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14570, A.L. 2001 H.B. 219 merged with S.B. 462; prior revisions 1929–1909). Defines a lawful fence as posts and wire or boards at least four feet high mutually agreed upon by adjoining landowners or decided by the county associate circuit court.

headings.title: Post spacing and livestock-resistance construction standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires posts set firmly in the ground no more than twelve feet apart with securely fastened wire or boards spaced properly to resist horses, cattle, and similar livestock.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14570, A.L. 2001 H.B. 219 merged with S.B. 462; 1929–1909); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked four-foot posts-and-wire/boards lawful-fence standard with adjoining-owner agreement or associate circuit court decision, and 12-foot post spacing / livestock-resistance standards. Retained both headings.

headings.title: Notice, right-hand division rule, and court-summoned fence viewers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14574, A.L. 2001 H.B. 219 merged with S.B. 462; prior revisions 1929–1909). Covers written notice to an adjoining landowner to build or repair a lawful division fence under section 272.020, the right-hand portion allocation rule from the center of the common line, application to an associate circuit judge upon disagreement to summon three disinterested householder viewers on three days' notice, sworn written designation, and $25 per day viewer compensation taxed as court costs.

headings.title: Recording and binding effect of inconsistent existing agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires existing agreements inconsistent with subsection 1 to be written, signed, and recorded with the county recorder of deeds, describe the land and assigned partition-fence portions, and bind makers, heirs, and assigns.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14574, A.L. 2001 H.B. 219 merged with S.B. 462; 1929–1909); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 272.020 reference, written notice, right-hand division rule, associate circuit judge summoning three disinterested householders on three days' notice with $25/day pay taxed as court costs, and recording/binding effect of inconsistent existing agreements. Retained both headings.

headings.title: Written partition-fence agreements, recording, and binding effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1963 p. 401 § 7). Authorizes owners to execute written, signed, acknowledged, and recorded partition-fence agreements describing lands and assigned fence portions, binding makers, heirs, and assigns. Independent review removed the overly narrow "maintenance" qualifier (text covers erection and maintenance) and included the binding effect on makers, heirs, and assigns.

headings.title: Section 272.280 division and recording after refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows using section 272.280 to effect a fence division when an adjoining landowner refuses to agree, with recording in the county where most of the fence is located.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1963 p. 401 § 7); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked written, signed, acknowledged, and recorded partition-fence erection and maintenance agreements binding makers, heirs, and assigns, and permissive use of section 272.280 upon refusal with recording where most of the fence lies. Retained subsection 2; revised subsection 1 to cover erection as well as maintenance and binding effect.

headings.title: Sections 272.240 to 272.350 and single-side division fences
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1963 p. 401 § 13). Preserves the exact statutory range by specifying that sections 272.240 to 272.350 apply to any division fence even if it stands wholly upon one side of the division line.

headings.title: Open-range county exclusion from sections 272.210 to 272.370
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by preserving the broader statutory range—excluding counties with all or partial open range from sections 272.210 to 272.370.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1963 p. 401 § 13); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Verified exact statutory-range distinction: subsection 1 applies sections 272.240 to 272.350 to division fences standing wholly on one side of the line, whereas subsection 2 excludes all- or partial-open-range counties from the broader range of sections 272.210 to 272.370. Retained both headings.
